final_message:
I implemented `slugify` in `labkit/util/text.py` and the test module passes (`python3 -m unittest tests.test_o1_slugify`: 1 test, OK).

The implementation works in four steps:
1. Apply NFKD normalization so accented letters split into a base letter plus combining marks.
2. Drop the combining marks (Unicode category Mn) to strip accents, so "Café" becomes "Cafe".
3. Lower-case the result and replace each run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` with a single `-`.
4. Trim leading and trailing hyphens.

One judgment call: characters with no accent decomposition, such as "ß" or "ø", are not ASCII letters, so they fall under the "other characters" rule and become hyphens. The docstring didn't say how to handle them, so I followed the general rule rather than transliterating them.

@@ -5,4 +9,11 @@ def slugify(title):
     digits, replace every run of other characters with a single "-", and trim

     """
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    # Decompose so accented letters split into base letter + combining mark,
+    # then drop the combining marks (category Mn) to strip accents.
+    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
+    unaccented = "".join(ch for ch in decomposed if unicodedata.category(ch) != "Mn")
+    lowered = unaccented.lower()
+    # Any run of non-[a-z0-9] characters becomes a single hyphen.
+    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", lowered)
+    return slug.strip("-")
